justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across time horizons, starting near 222.5 for the one-day forecast and gradually rising to 230 at the one-month horizon. The one-day estimate was anchored primarily by recent price action and short-term momentum, assuming no major overnight catalyst would dramatically shift the market. The one-week estimate of 225 incorporates a slight continuation of that trend while acknowledging mean-reversion forces that could temper any strong directional move. The one-month estimate of 230 reflects a longer-run bullish bias, likely grounded in broader macroeconomic conditions, earnings expectations, or sector trends that were supportive at the time of the forecast, while still remaining close to the nearer-term levels to avoid overconfidence in sustained momentum.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the time horizon extends, which is a standard reflection of compounding uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval of 210 to 235 is relatively tight, since intraday and overnight moves are constrained by typical volatility patterns. By one week, the interval opens to 200–250, capturing the possibility of a significant news event, earnings surprise, or macro data release shifting sentiment meaningfully in either direction. At one month, the interval of 185–275 acknowledges that a full range of fundamental and technical scenarios could plausibly materialize, including trend reversals, sector rotations, or broader market corrections.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside even these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data, an unexpected Federal Reserve policy shift, or a geopolitical shock could drive prices well below 185 within a month. On the upside, a blowout earnings report, a surprise dovish pivot, or a short squeeze dynamic could push prices meaningfully above 275. Liquidity conditions and broader equity market volatility also play a role — if overall market implied volatility spikes, individual name moves can far exceed historical norms. These tail scenarios were intentionally left outside the 90% interval but are worth monitoring closely as conditions evolve.
